text.en: How did Richard Ebright become a scientist? A boy collecting butterflies and a mother who helped.

The piece is by Robert W. Peterson about Richard Ebright, a boy who loved butterflies.
As a child Ebright collected butterflies and learned their names. His mother encouraged his interest.
His mother gave him a book called The Travels of Monarch X, about monarch butterflies' migration to Central America.
The book invited readers to help tag butterflies for research by Dr Urquhart of the University of Toronto, and Ebright joined.
He was a straight-A student and also took part in debating and the Model United Nations.
His social studies teacher, Mr Weiherer, opened his mind to new ideas and admired his hard work.
Ebright was competitive, but he wanted to do the best job, not win just for a prize.
The ingredients of a scientist include curiosity, parents' support, a good teacher and hard work.

problem.en: Ebright studied for 3 hours each night for 5 nights. How many hours?

why.en: The teacher said three or four hours; practice only.

prompt.en: List what made Ebright a scientist.

points.en: His mother and teacher helped him.
Curiosity and effort make a scientist.
